sn35.63:1.2: Then the Venerable Migajāla approached the Blessed One, paid homage to him, sat down to one side,
sn35.63:1.4: “Venerable sir, it is said, ‘a lone dweller, a lone dweller.’
sn35.63:1.5: In what way, venerable sir, is one a lone dweller, and in what way is one dwelling with a partner?”
sn35.63:2.1: “There are, Migajāla, forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.63:2.2: If a bhikkhu seeks delight in them, welcomes them, and remains holding to them,
sn35.63:2.4: When there is delight, there is infatuation.
sn35.63:2.5: When there is infatuation, there is bondage.
sn35.63:2.6: Bound by the fetter of delight, Migajāla, a bhikkhu is called one dwelling with a partner.
sn35.63:2.7: “There are, Migajāla, sounds cognizable by the ear … odours cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tactile objects cognizable by the body …
sn35.63:2.8: mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.63:2.9: If a bhikkhu seeks delight in them …
sn35.63:2.13: he is called one dwelling with a partner.
sn35.63:2.14: “Migajāla, even though a bhikkhu who dwells thus resorts to forests and groves, to remote lodgings where there are few sounds and little noise, desolate, hidden from people, appropriate for seclusion,
sn35.63:2.15: he is still called one dwelling with a partner.
sn35.63:2.17: Because craving is his partner, and he has not abandoned it;
sn35.63:2.18: therefore he is called one dwelling with a partner.
sn35.63:3.1: “There are, Migajāla, forms cognizable by the eye that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.63:3.2: If a bhikkhu does not seek delight in them, does not welcome them, and does not remain holding to them,
sn35.63:3.4: When there is no delight, there is no infatuation.
sn35.63:3.5: When there is no infatuation, there is no bondage.
sn35.63:3.6: Released from the fetter of delight, Migajāla, a bhikkhu is called a lone dweller.
sn35.63:3.7: “There are, Migajāla, sounds cognizable by the ear … odours cognizable by the nose … tastes cognizable by the tongue … tactile objects cognizable by the body …
sn35.63:3.8: mental phenomena cognizable by the mind that are desirable, lovely, agreeable, pleasing, sensually enticing, tantalizing.
sn35.63:3.9: If a bhikkhu does not seek delight in them …
sn35.63:3.13: he is called a lone dweller.
sn35.63:3.14: “Migajāla, even though a bhikkhu who dwells thus lives in the vicinity of a village, associating with bhikkhus and bhikkhunīs, with male and female lay followers, with kings and royal ministers, with sectarian teachers and their disciples,
sn35.63:3.15: he is still called a lone dweller.
sn35.63:3.17: Because craving is his partner, and he has abandoned it;
sn35.63:3.18: therefore he is called a lone dweller.”
